title: Generic (fallback for any other deliverable)
covers: Any deliverable no other lens fits. Derive its professional bar first; use a closer lens as well whenever one partly fits.

stakeholders.who: The person this deliverable is made for (work out who that is first)
cares_about: they can use it without help
would_notice: something that works but is not what they asked for
an error or empty screen with no explanation

stakeholders.who: A professional in this field reviewing the work
cares_about: the work meets the field's normal standard
would_notice: 'done' with nothing to show for it
a weakness hidden instead of named
a beginner's mistake any professional in the field would spot

stakeholders.who: Whoever has to run, change or hand on this work next
cares_about: knowing what was checked and what was not
would_notice: no note of what was verified
a key or password in the files

first_ten_seconds: Who is this for, and what would they do with it first?
Use or open it cold as that person: what are the first three things you notice?
Does anything look unfinished, broken or like a template?

checks.claim: Before reviewing, the professional bar for this kind of deliverable is written down: who uses it, what good looks like, what breaks it.
checks.how_to_inspect: Write three short lists (users, signs of good work, typical failures) from the brief and, where needed, sourced research; mark them provisional.
checks.evidence_required: The three lists in the review.

source.quote: derive its professional bar (who uses it, what good looks like, what breaks it)

checks.claim: The first-ten-seconds test was done cold, as the primary user: what they see, understand and would do first.
checks.how_to_inspect: Open or use the deliverable as that person would, without prior knowledge, and write down the first three things you notice.
checks.evidence_required: The three observations and what each led to.

checks.claim: Every visible detail was checked from that person's point of view: spacing, alignment, contrast, copy, empty and error states, naming, units.
checks.how_to_inspect: Go through the deliverable part by part with that list and write each finding down.
checks.evidence_required: The findings per part, with screenshots or excerpts.

source.quote: Check every visible detail from that person's point of view

checks.claim: No test mode, mock backend, sample data or placeholder content is left in what is handed over.
checks.how_to_inspect: Search the deliverable for test, mock, sample, lorem, todo and example, and look at every visible value.
checks.evidence_required: The search command and its output (zero hits, or each hit fixed).

source.quote: No test mode, mock backend, or fake/sample data left in.

checks.claim: The deliverable matches what the person actually asked for, not a technically nearby substitute.
checks.how_to_inspect: Put the original request next to the result and check every asked-for item.
checks.evidence_required: The request items with where each is met, or why it is not.

source.quote: The delivered design matches the user's actual stated intent, not a technically-adjacent substitute.

checks.claim: Every 'done', 'works' or 'tested' in the hand-off is backed by evidence; nothing is claimed that did not run.
checks.how_to_inspect: Mark each claim in the hand-off and attach the command, screenshot or file that proves it.
checks.evidence_required: The claim list with evidence per claim.

source.quote: Never claim a check, test, build, eval, live call, charge, install or deploy that did not run.

checks.claim: Whatever is still weak is fixed or named plainly in the hand-off: what it is, who would notice, and why it is not fixed now.
checks.how_to_inspect: Compare the review findings with the hand-off text and check every open finding appears there.

source.quote: Fix it, or say plainly what is still weak.

checks.claim: No secret sits in code, bundles, logs, error messages, documents or git; placeholders only.
checks.how_to_inspect: Search everything handed over for key, token, password and secret.
checks.evidence_required: The search command and its output (zero hits, or each hit fixed).

source.quote: never in code, client bundles, logs, error messages or git

checks.claim: The hand-off says what was verified and what was assumed, and lists open owner actions.
checks.how_to_inspect: Read the hand-off as the next person and check both lists are there.
checks.evidence_required: The verified, assumed and open lists.

source.quote: What was verified vs. assumed is stated explicitly.

common_sloppy_defects.symptom: the deliverable follows the pattern of another project type instead of what this one needs
'works' and 'tested' in the report with no command, screenshot or file behind it
a known problem left out of the hand-off, found later by the owner
sample data, mock responses or TODO notes in what was handed over
